_source: content-design-kit.md §6 is the house style and this file follows it: line one states the round's real fact, line two either asks the reader something or names what comes next. Voice: §2, register B. Every template is linted on every run against build/copy-rules.json.
_registers: TWO registers, split by what a post is FOR (owner call, 2026-09-02). ENGAGEMENT posts exist to be replied to and close on a question — matchday, matchdayFinal, question, podium, playerOfRound, teamOfWeek, topPlayers. captions.mjs holds that list and lifts the linter's trailing-question ban for exactly those. INFORMATIONAL posts exist to be acted on and point forward instead — buildUp, deadline, priceChanges, leagueTable, results, resultsFinal. `results` is informational on purpose: §6's «فريقك عمل كام؟» was retired, because asking a manager their score after a bad round is the one question that earns no reply.
_vars: {matches} is «ماتش واحد» / «ماتشين» / «3 ماتشات» for that day, already pluralised — Arabic counts one and two in the noun. {played} is the same for finished fixtures. {deadline} is «الاتنين 4 العصر». {gw} is «الجولة الرابعة». A caption carrying none of these would read identically in any gameweek, which is the failure the first version shipped.
_leagueTable: leagueTable deliberately carries no {gw}. It goes out on a MIDDLE day, before the round it is authored under has been played, so «ترتيب الدوري بعد الجولة الرابعة» would name a round that has not happened yet. The table is simply the table.
_settleDay: podium, playerOfRound, teamOfWeek and topPlayers were `needsHuman` until 2026-09-02, on the reasoning that a post naming a real person is taste. They are templated because the naming was never needed: the card already carries every name, club and score, so the caption asks instead. The names still go on the CARD verbatim, including a manager's team name our own style guide would reject.
